title: Laredo Regional Food Bank Marks 43 Years as LISD Culinary Students Cook World Food Day Luncheon
excerpt: The Laredo Regional Food Bank celebrated 43 years of serving Webb County with a World Food Day rice-and-beans luncheon cooked by culinary arts students from Martin, Nixon and Cigarroa high schools.
content:
Forty-three years of feeding Webb County got a celebration cooked up by the next generation. The Laredo Regional Food Bank marked World Food Day with a rice-and-beans luncheon on Friday, Oct. 16, at the Joe A. Guerra Laredo Public Library, according to Local National.

The meal itself was the point: culinary arts students from three Laredo ISD high schools — Martin, Nixon’s Mustang Kitchen and Cigarroa — did the cooking for the noon-to-2:30 p.m. gathering, according to the report.

Katie Nye, who directs the Hunger Free Community Accelerator at the Baylor Collaborative on Hunger and Poverty, delivered the keynote address, according to Local National. The accelerator works with communities across the country to build lasting ways to fight hunger.

The luncheon also marked the food bank’s 43rd year serving Webb County. Executive Director Jessica Martinez said the event was a chance to spotlight young culinary talent while the community comes together around food insecurity, according to the report. Methodist Healthcare Ministries and EOG Resources served as premier sponsors.

In a county where food insecurity touches thousands of families, the pairing on display — a food bank with four decades of service and high school students learning to feed their own community — is the kind of story worth pausing on.
